title: fix(plugin-security): a capability name collision now reaches the author
body:
Fixes #18023

Clause-②: yes

A package's **declared capability** was dropped on a capability-name collision and the drop reached nobody. The branch reported through `logger?.warn?.(…)` — optionally chained **twice** — so a caller that passed no logger produced no output at all, and the declaration vanished with one internal counter incremented. This module's own header called such a row "skipped loudly"; nothing about it was loud.

⛔ **The skip is unchanged.** Refusing to write into a `sys_capability` row another package owns is correct under ADR-0086 D4, and every case below asserts it still happens, still counts, still leaves the foreign row untouched, and still reports the name as materialized so the back-compat derivation does not clobber that row (#4967 Part 1). What changed is that the refusal is now legible to the author who caused it.

## Reproduced first, then measured again

Both runs drive a real collision through `bootstrapDeclaredCapabilities` with **no logger passed**, spying on all five console channels. The permission-set axis runs beside it in the same harness as the lit control.

| | before (`57343f761`, pre-change) | after (`9cbca2136`) |
|---|---|---|
| `skippedForeign` | 1 | **1** — unchanged |
| author-visible console lines | **0** | **1** |
| diagnostic records on outcome | `undefined` | 1 |
| LIT CONTROL — permission-set axis, same harness | 1 | 1 |
| DISCRIMINATING CONTROL — non-colliding pass that really seeds, updates, claims and leaves a row unchanged | — | **0 lines** |

The after line, verbatim:

```
warn: [security] [capability_name_collision] 1 declared capability was NOT applied — another
package already owns that capability name (ADR-0086 D4). The declaring package's authored label,
description and scope are NOT in effect, and the capability is attributed to the owning package.
{"event":"capability_name_collision","collisions":[{"name":"shared_cap","declaredBy":"com.example.b",
"ownedBy":"com.example.a","grantedBy":[],"fix":"Rename the capability in package \"com.example.b\" …"}]}
```

## The design choice: a parallel module, not an extension, and not a copy

The card asked for "its own diagnostic record type, its own key on the capability seeder's outcome, and its own pins — a second design rather than a mechanical copy". Measured against the shared machinery on `main`, four of the six things a collision report is made of are axis-**specific** here — the token, the record type, the wording and the consequence — so they live in a new `capability-name-collision.ts`. Folding them into a file named `permission-set-name-collision.ts` would make that name lie, and renaming that file churns pins that landed one card ago.

**The consequence really is different, and that is the reason this is not a copy.** On the permission-set axis the entire declared set is not materialized and none of its permissions are in effect. Here the name still **resolves** — the owning package's row answers for it. What is lost is narrower, and the diagnostic says so precisely: the declaring package's authored `label` / `description` / `scope` are not applied, and `sys_capability.package_id` attributes the capability to the other package, so the declaring package has no provenance claim over it. A message borrowing the sibling's wording would send the author hunting a broken grant that is not broken; a pin asserts that it does not (`expect(d.message).not.toContain('none of its object, field, tab')`).

⛔ **What is axis-independent is reused, never re-derived** — that is the drift this card exists to avoid:

- `permissionSetNameIsForeign` — THE owner-comparison predicate. The seeder's branch now routes through it instead of its own `existing.package_id === packageId`, so a **nullish owner reads FOREIGN on both axes by construction** (ADR-0086 D3), and a pin exercises exactly that row shape.
- `CollisionReportSink` — the minimal sink type, imported from the sibling and re-exported rather than structurally re-declared.

`reportPermissionSetNameCollisions` is deliberately **not** reused: its message states a permission-set consequence. Its sink discipline is restated, because that discipline is the contract this card buys rather than a derivation that can drift — and both axes pin it independently, including the `(logger?.warn ?? console.warn)(…)` receiver-detach trap (a class-based host sink that reaches for `this` is injected and must not throw).

`reportPermissionSetNameCollisions`'s judgement call, which the dispatch left to this lane: it does **not** generalise. It takes `readonly PermissionSetNameCollisionDiagnostic[]` and words a permission-set sentence, and an axis parameter threaded through it would produce one function that words two different consequences — the shape that makes both wrong.

## Reverse verification

Fix committed first (`aafc3ce26`), then the branch mutated back to the old `logger?.warn?.` form **and** the pass-end report deleted, on disk, from the committed state:

```
BASELINE HEAD blob hash = 3cb4ec4a3ce5d6983fa6ca5e3fda13bd0e8ca926
anchor counts BEFORE:  capabilityNameCollisionDiagnostic({ = 1   logger?.warn?.('[security] capability name owned = 0
anchor counts AFTER:   capabilityNameCollisionDiagnostic({ = 0   logger?.warn?.('[security] capability name owned = 1
MUTATED  blob hash     = 0b2ec0f476ccad54c39d8fa003dfd256081da91f   (differs ⇒ the mutation really landed)
→ Tests  4 failed | 39 passed (43)
restore: git checkout HEAD -- THE-FILE;  git diff HEAD → empty;  hash back to 3cb4ec4a3…
```

The direction is **turns red**, and the four that redden are exactly the four that assert output. The fifth — the no-collision silence control — stays **green** under the ablation, which is correct and is the point: a mute seeder also prints nothing on a non-colliding pass, so that case is discriminating in the other direction only.

## Clause-② re-derivation — `yes`, with a discriminating control

Re-derived from the **delivered** diff, not carried from the claim. The new symbols are re-exported from `src/index.ts`, and `package.json` publishes `exports["."] → ./dist/index.{js,mjs,d.ts}` with `files: ["dist", …]`, so the test is reachability from the **built** entry:

```
                                            dist/index.d.ts  dist/index.js  dist/index.mjs
CAPABILITY_NAME_COLLISION                          5              6              5
capabilityNameCollisionDiagnostic                  2              4              3
formatCapabilityNameCollisionDiagnostic            2              3              2
reportCapabilityNameCollisions                     3              4              3
CapabilityNameCollisionDiagnostic (type)           5              3              2
permissionSetNameIsForeign  (POSITIVE control —
  a symbol known published before this diff)       4              5              4
nonexistentSymbolXyz18023   (NEGATIVE control)     0              0              0
```

Both controls behave, so the probe discriminates. New exported symbols on a published entry ⇒ **`Clause-②: yes`**, and the changeset is graded **`minor`** accordingly (a `patch` with `yes` is refused, #16361). `needs:contract-review` is carried on this PR and on the card.

`CapabilitySeedOutcome.collisions` is the other limb the claim predicted; it is **not** what decides `yes` here, because `bootstrapDeclaredCapabilities` is not itself re-exported from `index.ts` — measured, not assumed. The `index.ts` re-exports are what carry it.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security test` — **113 files / 2181 tests, all passing**.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security typecheck` — clean (`tsc --noEmit`, scripts project, and `check:test-typecheck`: 0 files / 0 errors).
- `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/plugin-security...' build` — closure green; the dist probe above is taken from that build.
- Gates run locally and their four-number reconciliation are in the report on the card.

Two existing `bootstrap-seed-round-trips` cases pinned this refusal's loudness by matching the **prose** `"owned by another package"`. They now match the stable `capability_name_collision` grep token and additionally assert the record on the pass outcome — a strictly stronger observable, and one that does not re-red on every rewording. ⛔ No test was skipped, quarantined or weakened.

## Acceptance notes

- **Not filed, noted:** `permissionSetNameIsForeign` carries the axis it was first written for in its name, and the capability seeder now imports it. Renaming it to something axis-neutral is a breaking change to a published export and buys only readability — a naming nit, excluded from the file-a-card classes. The import site documents why one name for one derivation beats two.
- **Not filed, noted:** the sibling axis states its refusal direction as "nothing is over-granted". This record deliberately makes the narrower claim — closed for the *declaration*, because nothing of the declaring package's is written anywhere — and says nothing about the owner's retained `scope`. Measured: the only non-test readers of `sys_capability` rows in this tree are the two seeders, the object definition, `security-plugin.ts` and `packages/lint`, and none was found reading a row's `scope` column for an authorization decision (capability `scope` is read off the spec-level `PLATFORM_CAPABILITIES` declaration instead). That is an observation about today's readers, ⛔ not a proof of absence, which is exactly why the record's severity note routes a future over-grant path to its own card rather than pre-judging it here.
- **Not filed, noted:** `cleanupPackagePermissions` covers `sys_permission_set` and does not touch `sys_capability`, so uninstalling the owning package does not currently remove the row. The wording avoids claiming a disappearing capability for exactly this reason.
- A separate finding for the **remaining** doubly-optional refusal branches in the two seeders is filed on the card's report; it is the same defect class one branch over and is deliberately not ridden in here, for the same reason this card was not ridden into #17516.
